Plain-text and Markdown accessors

Source: R/acc_sacha_format.R
accessors-sacha.Rd

Functions that retrieve data for a single taxon are provided in two variants: a plain-text accessor, intended for interactive inspection in the console, and a Markdown accessor with the suffix _md, intended for document rendering (Quarto or R Markdown). Both variants read the same cached record and differ only in output format and in the handling of missing data and connection failures.

Function pairs

  • first_publicacion() and first_publicacion_md()

  • classification() and classification_md()

  • common_names() and common_names_md()

  • syn_and_comb() and syn_and_comb_md()

  • references_sp() and references_sp_md()

  • indexations() and indexations_md()

  • sc_full_name() and sc_full_name_md()

The platform shortcuts documented in indexations() (for example gbif_url()) follow the plain-text behavior described below.

Plain-text accessors

Plain-text accessors return a character string of class sacha_text. When printed, the text is shown as written, with one line per line break, without quotation marks, element indices or escape sequences. The object behaves as an ordinary character string in paste(), as.character() and comparisons. For missing data and failures:

  • When the source returns no data, a localized no-data message is returned.

  • When a connection failure prevents retrieval, an R warning() is raised and a localized connection message is returned.

indexations() and the platform shortcuts are the exception to the return type: they return a named character vector of URLs, which is empty when no URL is available, and raise a warning when that absence is caused by a connection failure. sc_full_name() never warns: if the name cannot be resolved, it returns species as given.

Markdown accessors

Markdown accessors write the Markdown string to the console with cat() so that it is inserted as-is in chunks with results = "asis", and return the same string invisibly. For missing data and failures:

  • An empty string ("") is returned invisibly, and nothing is written, when no data are available. Sections without data are therefore omitted from the document.

  • No R warning() is raised, including on connection failures.

Scientific names are written in italics, special Markdown characters are escaped, and grouped content (synonyms, references) is written as bulleted lists.

Shared behavior

Both variants use the same per-species cache for the duration of the R session (see sacha_clear_cache()) and the same configuration (see sacha_configure()). The language argument affects only labels and messages, never the data. Invalid arguments (a species that is not a binomial, an unsupported language, an unknown rank or identifier, or a non-logical save_bib) raise an error in both variants. The sc_full_name() pair has an independent cache and always queries the Catalogue of Life dataset "3LXR".

Shared export directory

Files explicitly saved by package functions are organised under sacha_exports inside the relevant base directory, which defaults to the current working directory. Taxon-specific outputs use sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species; GBIF crop exports add a place subdirectory, while iNaturalist photographs, metadata and compositions are stored in sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species/inat. Taxon-level BibTeX references and GBIF occurrence data and maps remain in the taxon directory. A complete ChecklistBank dataset is not taxon-specific, so its archive and download metadata are stored in sacha_exports/checklistbank_<dataset>.

In functions with a directory, images_directory, or bib_dir argument, that value is the base directory under which sacha_exports is created or searched. The argument documentation identifies the resulting path for each function. Existing spatial occurrence exports in spatial_exports and iNaturalist archives in images remain readable through the local-source functions; new package exports use sacha_exports.

Figures created only to render a Markdown report are written to the format-specific paths managed by Quarto or R Markdown. These intermediate assets are kept separate so that simultaneous rendering to multiple output formats does not cause one format to overwrite another. Persistent map PNGs are saved under sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species; iNaturalist compositions are saved under sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species/inat.

Choosing between them

Use the plain-text accessors to inspect a taxon interactively or to obtain a value for further computation. Use the Markdown accessors to assemble reports of one or several taxa, where unavailable data must be omitted without interrupting rendering.
